request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
All four e2e tests pass now.

The change is entirely in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/Sheets.java`, in `nextClaimNumber`:

- **Shared sequence:** when a claim is opened, the app finds the sheet's whole tree. That's the top sheet of its parent chain plus every sheet below that top sheet, at any depth, so sibling sheets share the sequence too. The claim gets the highest "last number given" across those sheets plus one, and that becomes the opening sheet's new last number.
- **Old numbers stay:** numbers already given don't change. No data migration was needed, because each sheet's existing count of numbers given (`claim_numbers`) already records its last number.
- **No duplicates under concurrency:** the row of every sheet in the tree is locked, in sorted order, until the transaction ends. Two claims opened at the same moment anywhere in the tree can't get the same number.
- **Per-period numbering** (`P1-1`, `X-1`) is unchanged and still counts per sheet.

**Decision for you:** the app already has a narrower "tree" in `People.treeOf`, used to keep names unique: a sheet's ancestors and descendants, which leaves out siblings. I used the wider definition for numbering, because with the narrower one two sibling sheets could hand out the same number, so the sequence wouldn't really be shared. The tests only use a single parent-to-child chain, so they don't separate the two definitions. If you want numbering to use the narrower one, it's a small change.

My first version failed the test because it never searched below the sheet doing the opening. I found that with temporary logging, fixed it, and removed the logging.
